summary: Morpheus comes back to himself in the office's rain, his eyes opening "dark and flashing with fire," and he rises, snapping his handcuffs as the Agents step into the next room. Agent Smith catches sight of Morpheus running past the open door and screams "Nooo!", firing a sweeping line of bullets across the sheetrocked wall. As Morpheus dives a bullet strikes his leg, sending him tumbling and knocks him off balance. Neo, judging "He won't make it," spins to snap a rope-end onto a bolted bar while Morpheus begins to fall. Neo hurls himself into the open space, the two bodies colliding mid-air, scrambling for a hold until the line snaps taut and breaks their embrace, sending Morpheus tumbling downward. Neo snatches hold of Morpheus's still handcuffed wrist and cries "Gotcha!"

what_changes.after: Revived and in motion, running and diving for the window to escape.

event_hint.one_line: Morpheus bolts for the window and Neo leaps after him in a mid-air rescue as Agent Smith opens fire.

uncertain: Whether the two Agents who entered the adjoining room are Smith's companions or replacements for the ones previously shot.
Whether Neo and Morpheus ultimately survive the fall after the scene ends on "Gotcha!"

minds.wants: To get his body moving and out of the Agents' reach before they can take him again — the window and the fall are simply the direction of escape.
minds.feels: A hard, recovered will flooding back into a body that has just been through whatever the Agents did to him; the "dark and flashing with fire" eyes read as rage and purpose rekindled at once, not calm.
minds.shows: Only the physical facts — lifting his face, rising, snapping the cuffs, running, diving. He gives no word or look to anyone; his interior is entirely consumed by motion.
minds.basis: The text marks the return as deliberate ('Slowly, Morpheus lifts his face'; eyes 'again dark and flashing with fire') and immediately converts it to action ('He rises. breaking his restraints the moment the Agents burst in change axes (condition, safety, custody) confirm he moves from passive prisoner to escape in seconds.

believes_about.belief: That Smith is a threat to be outrun, not reasoned with or acknowledged.

minds.wants: To stop Morpheus from getting away — to re-seize the prisoner who is the point of the whole operation.
minds.feels: Fury and, underneath it, a loss of control that he will not permit. The scream 'Nooo!' is not tactical; it is the crack in the composed agent who was gunned down in sc-166 and is now back and humiliated, and letting the One's mentor slip past him again is intolerable.
minds.shows: The vocal break ('Nooo!') and the sweeping line of fire — a wide, area-denial burst rather than a careful aimed shot, which is exactly what a man trying to cut off a runner rather than kill cleanly would do.
minds.basis: He 'Smith halts, watching Morpheus dash through the doorway.' and immediately screams and he unleashes a continuous stream of gunfire that carves a straight, unbroken path across the drywall.' The sweep, not a single kill-shot, signals a desperate attempt to intercept. Earlier, in sc-166, Smith was shot down by Neo and now confronts Morpheus escaping — the continuity of a thwarted captor.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus is a captive he can still pin down and retake.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus has already freed himself (snapped the cuffs) and is committed to the window and the fall; Smith is reacting to an escape already in progress, not controlling a prisoner.

minds.wants: To get Morpheus out alive — to convert his rooftop firepower (sc-166) into a physical rescue when the escape goes wrong.
minds.feels: A cold, fast calculation under pressure: he judges the odds ('He won't make it') and then overrides that judgment with commitment, hurling himself after Morpheus. The shift from assessment to self-endangerment is the whole of his arc in the scene.
minds.shows: Two clean beats — the muttered verdict, then whip-crack motion (snapping the rope to the bar and leaping). He shows no panic, only decisive action, and the closing 'Gotcha!' is effort and relief, not bravado.
minds.basis: His line 'He won't make it' is stated as a judgment immediately before he 'spins, every move a whip crack' to rig the rope and 'he launches into the vast blue expanse.' The change axis (resolve: doubting -> committing) tracks this. In sc-166 he was already trying to 'will him into action' and had attached the rope to his harness — the rescue is prepared, not improvised from nothing.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus cannot survive the leap on his own and needs to be caught.
That Smith's fire is the immediate lethal problem to beat, not a puzzle to solve.

connects_back: sc-166: Neo gunned down the Agents (Smith among them) and, in the same breath, attached the climbing rope to his harness while trying to rouse Morpheus — this scene is the payoff of that preparation.
sc-166: Morpheus was left slumped and unresponsive after the firefight; his 'coming back' here answers Neo's 'Get up, Morpheus!'
The Agents' return from being shot (Smith screaming and firing again) continues the established rule that they regenerate and resume the pursuit.
sets_up: ev-030: Morpheus surviving and being hauled to safety is what allows the group to reach the subway-station phone-booth exit, where Smith ambushes them.
ev-030: Neo's mid-air self-sacrificing grab prefigures Trinity's confession of love to Neo and the crew's deepening faith in him.
The wound to Morpheus's leg and the still-fastened handcuffs raise the stakes for the escape that must carry an injured man to the exit.
dramatic_function: To convert the rooftop victory (the Agents gunned down) into a fresh, physical jeopardy — the rescue set-piece — and to reposition Neo from the doubter on the machine gun to the man who bets his own body on Morpheus, so the film's faith-in-Neo arc can keep climbing.
